newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - July 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - July 24.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Law enforement agents acknowledge that the government lacks evidence to pin down and prosecute an alleged drug lord (MANILA TIMES)
- Two out of three Philippine school children are unable to find their own country on the map (MANILA TIMES)
- Laos, Burma join ASEAN while Cambodia welcomed efforts by the group to mediate in the country's political crisis (ALL PAPERS)
- Police say evidence mounts that policemen assigned to a leading senator were linked to a suspected drug baron (ALL PAPERS)
- Metro Manila's traffic chief suggests banning private cars with less than three passengers from major roads. (ALL PAPERS)
- President Fidel Ramos called for a stepped-up campaign to curb population growth, noting that at the current rate the Philippine population would double in 30 years. (PHILIPPINE STAR)
- The central bank issues new guidelines to curb speculation against the Philippine peso (ALL PAPERS).
- The fall in the peso is likely to reduce the country's trade deficit to 10 billion pesos, according to Economic Planning Secretary Cielito Habito (BUSINESS WORLD)
- The Department of Agriculture said there is no need for rice imports despite one prediction it would have to because of the likely impact of the El Nino weather phenomenon. (ALL PAPERS)

- The Philippines risks jarring relations with its trading partners because of a court decision suspending low-tariff imports of agricultural goods, Agricluture Secretary Salvador Escudero said (BUSINESS WORLD)
- President Fidel Ramos approves the sale of the government's 60 percent stake in a geothermal company.
- Manila's soon-to-be privatised water and sewerage company will not put up charges because of the recent fall in the peso, one of the new concessionaries said (MANILA TIMES)
